subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Gas Turbine Power Plants
description: Learn Gas Turbine Power Plants in one minute.

hook.text: A gas turbine power plant can start generating electricity in under ten minutes. Coal plants take hours.

buildup.text: Natural gas burns in a combustor. Hot exhaust spins a turbine connected to a generator at 3,600 RPM.

discovery.text: Gas turbines are compact, fast-starting, and relatively clean. They produce less carbon dioxide per watt than coal.

twist.text: Turbine blades face 1,400°C — above their melting point. Internal cooling channels keep the metal from melting.

climax.text: Peaker plants fire up gas turbines during demand spikes. They fill the gap that solar and wind can't cover.

punchline.text: Fast start. Clean burn. The grid's best backup plan.

quiz.question: How do gas turbine blades survive temperatures above their melting point?
options: They are coated with diamond that has a higher melting temperature
Internal cooling channels circulate air to keep blade metal below its limit
The turbine spins so fast that heat doesn't have time to accumulate
